title: Nuclear Physics and Radioactive Decay
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Physics: Nuclear Physics Worksheets
standard_text: Radioactive decay (half-life, decay constant, activity and exponential decay), the inverse square law for gamma radiation, nuclear radius, mass and energy, binding energy, and alpha and beta decay equations.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level physics worksheets on nuclear physics: half-life, decay constant, activity, nuclear radius, binding energy per nucleon, decay equations and the inverse square law. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A = λN and λ = ln 2 / T½.
key_sub: Binding energy comes from the mass defect: E = Δm c².
body_html:
How to think about it

Radioactive decay is random but follows N = N₀e−λt, with λ = ln 2/T½ and activity A = λN. Use seconds when finding λ in s⁻¹.

The nucleus has radius R = r₀A1/3. Its mass is less than the mass of its separate nucleons; this mass defect × c² is the binding energy (1 u = 931.5 MeV).

Example

T½ = 8.0 days. λ?

8.0 days = 6.91 × 105 s

0.693 ÷ 6.91 × 105

Answer: 1.00 × 10−6 s⁻¹

Example

Activity 800 Bq, 3 half-lives later?

800 ÷ 2³

Answer: 100 Bq

Common mistakes

  • Using days in A = λN without converting to seconds.
  • Dividing by the number of half-lives instead of by 2 each time.
  • Getting Z wrong in β⁻ decay (it goes up by 1).

faq.a: The probability per second that a nucleus decays: λ = ln 2 / T½.
The energy needed to separate a nucleus into its protons and neutrons, equal to the mass defect × c².
